text_es: The entry function `evaluate(hand)` receives a list of five tuples, where each tuple contains an integer value and a suit character. Determine the rank of the poker hand using explicit rules. Check if all suits are identical to identify a flush. Check if the values form a consecutive sequence to identify a straight. If both apply, it is a straight flush. Otherwise, group the values to count frequencies. Check if there are four identical values for a four of a kind. Check if there is a three of a kind and a pair for a full house. Check for a standalone three of a kind, two pairs, or a single pair. Return an integer from one to nine representing the hand strength, where nine is a straight flush and one is a high card.

The entry function `score(rolls)` receives a list of integers representing the number of pins knocked down in a bowling game. Iterate through the rolls using a loop to calculate the total score for exactly ten frames. Determine if a roll is a strike by checking if ten pins were knocked down in a single roll, which adds the next two rolls to the frame score. Otherwise, check if two consecutive rolls in a frame add up to ten to identify a spare, which adds the next single roll to the score. If neither a strike nor a spare occurs, simply add the two rolls of the frame. Check if the frame index reaches ten to stop processing regular frames and handle the bonus rolls correctly.

The entry function `withdraw(amount)` receives an integer representing the requested withdrawal amount. The machine holds one hundred, fifty, twenty, ten, five, and one dollar bills. Loop through these available denominations from largest to smallest. While the remaining amount is greater than or equal to the current denomination, subtract the denomination from the amount and increment a counter for that bill. Check if the requested amount is exactly zero at any point to stop the loop early. Check if the requested amount is negative or if it cannot be exactly dispensed, returning an empty list in those cases. Otherwise, return a list of six integers representing the count of each dispensed bill.

The entry function `vend(coins)` receives a list of integers representing inserted coin values in cents. The goal is to purchase an item costing seventy five cents. Loop through the coins and add them to a running total only if they are valid values of five, ten, or twenty five cents. If a coin is invalid, ignore it. Check if the total reaches or exceeds seventy five cents to stop accepting coins immediately. Once dispensing, check if change is required. Calculate how many quarters, dimes, and nickels to return by repeatedly checking if the change due is greater than or equal to the coin value and subtracting it. Return a tuple containing the purchased status as a boolean and a list of returned change coins.

The entry function `match(pattern)` receives a string pattern and returns a helper function that takes a target string to evaluate. The pattern supports standard characters, a period to match any single character, and an asterisk to match zero or more of the preceding character. Iterate through the target string and the pattern simultaneously. Check if the next pattern character is an asterisk, and if so, explore both the case where the preceding character is skipped and the case where it consumes a matching character. Check if the pattern character is a period, which successfully consumes any character. Otherwise, verify that the literal characters match exactly, returning a boolean indicating success.

The entry function `validate(date)` receives a string representing a date in year month day format separated by hyphens. Extract the numeric components and verify they form a valid calendar date. Check if the month falls between one and twelve. Determine if the year is a leap year by checking if it is divisible by four, while also checking that it is not divisible by one hundred unless it is also divisible by four hundred. Check if the day is valid for the given month, explicitly checking for months with thirty one days, months with thirty days, and February. Return a boolean indicating if the provided date is strictly valid.

The entry function `analyze(password)` assesses the strength of a provided string password. Iterate through every character in the password to analyze its composition. Check if the character is an uppercase letter, a lowercase letter, a numeric digit, or a special punctuation mark, updating a separate flag for each. Check if the total length is at least eight characters, and provide a bonus point if it exceeds twelve characters. Check if the password consists entirely of letters or entirely of numbers to deduct points. Return an integer score from zero to seven based on how many of these conditional checks are satisfied.

The entry function `navigate(instructions)` receives a list of characters representing commands for a robot on a grid. The robot starts at origin facing north. Iterate through each command in the sequence. Determine if the command is a forward move, and if so, check the current facing direction to update either the vertical or horizontal position accordingly. Check if the command is a left turn to rotate the cardinal direction counterclockwise. Check if the command is a right turn to rotate the direction clockwise. Check if the command is to wait, which does nothing. Check if an unknown command appears, and if so, stop processing immediately. Return a tuple of the final coordinates.

The entry function `compress(text)` takes a string of alphabetical characters and returns its compressed representation. Initialize an empty result list and a counter. Iterate through the characters of the string using a loop. Check if the current character is identical to the previous character to increment the counter. If the character is different, check if the counter is greater than one to append the count and the previous character to the result, or just the character if the count is exactly one. After the loop finishes, check if there are remaining characters and append the last accumulated character and its count. Return the concatenated result string.

The entry function `calculate(income)` receives a floating point number representing an annual income and calculates the total tax owed. The tax system uses many progressive brackets. Check if the income exceeds two hundred fifty thousand to apply a forty percent rate to the excess. Check if the remaining income exceeds one hundred fifty thousand to apply a thirty five percent rate. Check thresholds for one hundred thousand, seventy five thousand, fifty thousand, twenty five thousand, and ten thousand, applying decreasing percentage rates to each slice. Any income below ten thousand is not taxed. Sum the calculated amounts from all applicable brackets and return the total tax rounded to two decimal places.

The entry function `evaluate(board)` receives a list of three lists, each containing three strings that are either empty, ex, or oh. Check all three horizontal rows to see if any row contains three identical non empty symbols. Check all three vertical columns in the same manner. Check the two main diagonals to determine if either has three matching symbols. If any of these directional conditions are met, return the winning symbol. If no winner is found, iterate through all cells using nested loops to check if any empty spaces remain. Return a draw status string if the board is completely full, or a pending status if empty spaces exist.

The entry function `convert(number)` takes an integer between one and three thousand nine hundred ninety nine and converts it to a roman numeral string. Use a loop to repeatedly subtract the largest possible roman numeral values while building the string. Check if the number is greater than or equal to one thousand to append a thousand symbol. Check if the number is greater than or equal to nine hundred to append a nine hundred symbol. Continue checking specific thresholds for five hundred, four hundred, one hundred, ninety, fifty, forty, ten, nine, five, and four. Subtract the respective amount each time a condition is met until the number reaches zero.

The entry function `paginate(current)` receives the current page number and the total number of pages as integers, and returns a list of strings representing page links to display. Check if the current page is less than one or greater than the total, returning an error string. Check if the total pages are less than or equal to seven, in which case return all pages. Otherwise, check if the current page is within the first four pages to show the first five pages, an ellipsis, and the last page. Check if the current page is within the last four pages to show the first page, an ellipsis, and the last five pages. If none apply, show the first page, an ellipsis, the current page and its neighbors, another ellipsis, and the last page.

The entry function `validate(move)` receives a tuple containing the starting and ending coordinates of a pawn move. Check if the piece is white to evaluate upward board movement. For a white pawn, check if the move is a single step forward into an empty square, or check if it is a double step forward from the second rank. Check if the move is a diagonal capture of a black piece to the left or right. For a black piece, evaluate the downward movement by checking if it moves a single step forward, check if it moves a double step from the seventh rank, or check if it captures diagonally. Return a boolean indicating whether the proposed move strictly follows all pawn rules.

The entry function `tokenize(text)` processes a string containing a simplified data serialization format and returns a list of string tokens. Iterate through each character using a while loop. Check if the character is a curly brace or square bracket to emit a structural token. Check if the character is a double quote to start reading a string literal, using an inner loop to read until the closing quote is found. Check if the character is a digit or a minus sign to read a numeric sequence. Check if the character is a space, tab, or newline to safely ignore it. Return the final list of extracted tokens.

The entry function `simulate(cars)` receives an integer representing the number of waiting cars. Simulate a traffic light cycle using a loop that decrements a timer. Check if the light is currently green, which allows two cars to pass per time step. Check if the light is yellow, which allows one car to pass only if fewer than two cars are left in the queue. Check if the light is red, during which no cars can pass. Check if an emergency vehicle override is active to immediately turn the light green for one step. Check when the timer for a state reaches zero to transition to the next color in the sequence. Return the total time steps required.

The entry function `pluralize(word)` receives a singular english noun as a string and returns its plural form. Check if the word is an irregular noun like child, mouse, tooth, foot, or person by matching exactly, and return the unique plural. Check if the word ends with a letter why preceded by a consonant, and if so, replace the why with ies. Check if the word ends with the letters ess, ex, zee, see aitch, or ess aitch, and if so, append es. Check if the word ends with an eff or eff ee, and replace the ending with ves. For all other standard cases, simply append an ess to the end of the word.

The entry function `route(requests)` manages an elevator receiving a list of requested floor integers. The elevator starts at floor zero. Loop through the requests to process them sequentially. Check if the requested floor is above the current floor to move the elevator up one floor at a time. Check if the requested floor is below the current floor to move the elevator down. During movement, check if any other pending requests fall exactly on the current floor to stop and service them immediately, removing them from the queue. Check if the elevator is already on the requested floor to just open the doors. Return a list of floors visited.

The entry function `format(table)` takes a list of strings representing an unaligned text table and aligns its columns. Iterate through all rows to split them by the pipe character and strip whitespace to find the maximum width of each column. Iterate through the rows again to construct the aligned output. Check if a row is a header separator row consisting only of hyphens, and pad it with dashes to match the maximum column width. Check if it is a standard data row, and pad the text with spaces. Check if a column is the very last one in the row to omit the trailing separator spacing. Return the joined table string.

The entry function `wrap(words)` receives a list of string words and an integer line length limit. Initialize an empty line and a list of output lines. Iterate through each word in the list. Check if adding the word to the current line would exceed the character length limit. If it does, check if the current line is completely empty, which implies the single word itself is longer than the limit. Check if this overly long word can be hyphenated by splitting it precisely at the limit. Otherwise, append the current line to the output and start a new line with the current word. Return a single string joined by newline characters.

Write a function `premiums(profiles)` that calculates car insurance costs. The input is a list of tuples containing driver age, number of accidents, and car type string. Process the list until a driver age of zero is encountered. The base rate is five hundred. If the age is under twenty five, add two hundred. If the age is over sixty five, add one hundred. If accidents are greater than two, deny coverage by returning zero for that profile. If there is one accident, add one hundred. If there are two accidents, add two hundred fifty. If the car type is sports, add three hundred. If the car type is minivan, subtract fifty. Return a list of final premium amounts. Example: an input of [(20, 1, 'sports'), (70, 3, 'sedan'), (0, 0, 'none')] should output [1100, 0].

Write a function `shipping(packages)` that estimates freight costs. The input is a list of tuples with weight in pounds, distance in miles, priority boolean, and international boolean. Process the list until a negative weight is found. The base rate is five. If weight is under two, the weight fee is zero. If weight is between two and ten, add three. If over ten, add ten. If distance is over one thousand, add five. If distance is over three thousand, add fifteen instead. If international is true, add a flat fee of fifty. Finally, if priority is true, double the entire calculated cost for that package. Return a list of costs. Example: input [(1, 500, False, False), (15, 3500, True, False), (-1, 0, False, False)] outputs [5, 60].

Write a function `penalty(reservations)` to process booking cancellations. The input is a list of tuples holding days notice, room rate, and membership level string. Stop evaluating if days notice is exactly nine hundred ninety nine. Memberships are basic, silver, and gold. Gold members always pay zero fee. Silver members pay half the room rate if notice is under three days, otherwise zero. Basic members pay the full rate if notice is under two days, half the rate if under seven days, and a flat twenty fee if under thirty days. Otherwise, basic members pay zero. Return a list of fee amounts. Example input: [(1, 100, 'basic'), (2, 200, 'silver'), (999, 0, 'none')] outputs [100, 100].

Write a function `baggage(bags)` to calculate luggage fees. The input is a list of tuples with weight in pounds, combined dimensions in inches, and passenger status string. Stop processing if weight is zero. Status can be none, elite, or crew. Crew members pay zero. Elite members get one free bag up to fifty pounds, but pay thirty if overweight. For status none, the standard fee is thirty for up to fifty pounds. If weight is between fifty and seventy pounds, the fee is an extra fifty. If weight is over seventy, the bag is not allowed so return negative one. If dimensions exceed sixty two inches, add an oversize fee of seventy five. Return a list of total fees. Example input: [(40, 50, 'elite'), (60, 70, 'none'), (0, 0, 'none')] outputs [0, 155].

Write a function `rewards(purchases)` to manage cafe rewards. The input is a list of transaction amounts. Loop through them until a negative transaction is found. For every whole dollar spent, earn one point. If the transaction is exactly five dollars, award two extra bonus points. If the transaction is over twenty dollars, multiply the base points earned for that transaction by two. Keep a running tally of points. Whenever total points reach or exceed one hundred, deduct one hundred points and add one free drink ticket. Return a tuple with total free drinks and remaining points. Example input: [25.50, 5.00, 80.00, -1] outputs (2, 17).

Write a function `thermostat(readings)` to control home temperature. The input is a list of tuples holding current temperature, target temperature, motion detected boolean, and windows open boolean. Stop processing if current temperature is zero. If windows are open, the action is off. If motion is detected, use the target temperature, else use the target minus five. If the current temperature is at least two degrees lower than the adjusted target, the action is heat. If current is at least two degrees higher than the adjusted target, the action is cool. Otherwise, the action is standby. Return a list of string actions. Example input: [(68, 72, True, False), (70, 72, False, False), (0, 0, False, False)] outputs ['heat', 'cool'].

Write a function `rebalance(assets)` to calculate asset trades. The input is a list of tuples with asset class string, current value, and target percentage as a decimal. Process until the asset class is the word stop. First, calculate the total portfolio value of all items before the stop word. Then loop through again. Calculate the current percentage for each asset. If the difference between current and target is less than five percent, the action is zero. If the asset class is bonds and the difference is less than ten percent, the action is zero. If the asset is cash, the action is zero. Otherwise, calculate the dollar amount to buy or sell to reach the exact target. Return a list of dollar amounts rounded to two decimals. Example input: [('stocks', 6000, 0.50), ('bonds', 4000, 0.50), ('stop', 0, 0)] outputs [-1000.0, 0.0].

Write a function `checkout(cart)` to calculate e-commerce totals. The input is a list of tuples with item name, price, category string, and clearance boolean. Stop processing if item name is done. For each item, apply rules to find its final price. If category is electronics, add a five dollar surcharge. If category is clothing and price is over fifty, apply ten percent off that item. If clearance is true, apply twenty percent off that item instead of the clothing discount (clearance takes precedence if both apply). Add the item's final price to a subtotal. After summing all items, if the subtotal is over two hundred, subtract twenty dollars. If under fifty, add ten dollars for shipping. Return the final total. Example input: [('shirt', 60, 'clothing', False), ('tv', 150, 'electronics', True), ('done', 0, '', False)] outputs 169.0.

Write a function `score(actions)` to evaluate puzzle performance. The input is a list of tuples with action type string and time in minutes. The starting score is one thousand. Stop processing if action type is escape. Action types are minor hint, major hint, and puzzle solved. A minor hint subtracts fifty points. A major hint subtracts one hundred fifty points. A puzzle solved adds fifty points. After processing all actions before escape, look at the time of the escape action. If this time exceeds sixty minutes, subtract ten points for every minute over sixty. If the score drops below zero at any point during calculation, reset it to zero. Return the final score. Example input: [('minor hint', 10), ('puzzle solved', 20), ('major hint', 40), ('escape', 65)] outputs 800.

Write a function `rank(matches)` to compute competitive ratings. The input is a list of tuples with result string, opponent rank, and disconnect boolean. The starting rank is one thousand. Stop processing if result is exit. Result can be win or loss. If disconnect is true, subtract fifty points regardless of the result string. If it is a win and no disconnect, add twenty points, plus an extra ten points if the opponent rank was higher than your current rank. If it is a loss and no disconnect, subtract twenty points, but only subtract ten if the opponent rank was higher. Your rank cannot exceed two thousand and cannot fall below zero. Return the final rank. Example input: [('win', 1200, False), ('loss', 900, False), ('win', 1000, True), ('exit', 0, False)] outputs 960.

Write a function `citations(offenses)` to evaluate driving violations. The input is a list of tuples with speed limit, actual speed, and zone type string. Process until speed limit is zero. Calculate the fine per offense. Speed up to five miles per hour over the limit is a warning with zero fine. Six to fifteen over is one hundred dollars. Sixteen to twenty five over is two hundred dollars. More than twenty five over is four hundred dollars. If the zone type is school, double the calculated fine. If the zone type is construction, add a flat one hundred dollars to the fine. Return a list of fine amounts. Example input: [(30, 34, 'regular'), (50, 70, 'school'), (60, 80, 'construction'), (0, 0, 'none')] outputs [0, 400, 300].

Write a function `invoice(logs)` to calculate contractor pay. The input is a list of tuples with hours worked, task type string, and rush boolean. Process until hours worked is zero. The standard rate is fifty per hour. Task types dictate base rates: consulting is standard, development is seventy five per hour, and design is sixty per hour. If rush is true, double the hourly rate for that specific log. If hours worked in a single log exceeds ten, the rate for the hours beyond ten is one point five times the applicable rate. Sum all logs and return the total invoice amount. Example input: [(5, 'development', False), (12, 'design', True), (0, 'none', False)] outputs 1995.0.

Write a function `tickets(orders)` to process concert sales. The input is a list of tuples with ticket type string, quantity, and promo code string. Stop if quantity is zero. Ticket types are general for fifty, vip for one hundred, and student for thirty. Calculate the subtotal. If quantity is five or more, apply a ten percent discount to the subtotal. Promo codes apply next: earlybird subtracts ten per ticket from the discounted total, while staff makes the entire order zero. Promo codes do not stack; staff takes priority, and earlybird only applies if the code is exactly earlybird. Return a list of final order prices. Example input: [('vip', 2, 'earlybird'), ('general', 6, 'none'), ('student', 1, 'staff'), ('none', 0, 'none')] outputs [180.0, 270.0, 0.0].

Write a function `gymnastics(routines)` to judge athletic events. The input is a list of tuples with difficulty score, execution score, fall count, and overtime boolean. Stop processing if difficulty is zero. The base score is difficulty plus execution. Subtract zero point five for each fall. If the fall count is three or more, subtract an extra full point penalty. If overtime is true, subtract zero point one. If the final calculated score exceeds twenty, cap it at exactly twenty. If the score is negative, set it to zero. Return a list of final scores rounded to one decimal place. Example input: [(10.0, 9.5, 1, False), (5.0, 5.0, 4, True), (15.0, 9.0, 0, False), (0, 0, 0, False)] outputs [19.0, 6.9, 20.0].

Write a function `water(readings)` to tally utility costs. The input is a list of tuples with gallons used, customer type string, and late payment boolean. Stop if gallons used is negative one. Customer types are residential and commercial. For residential, the first thousand gallons are free, the next four thousand are two cents per gallon, and anything over five thousand is five cents per gallon. For commercial, there is a base fee of fifty dollars, plus three cents per gallon for all gallons used. After calculating the base bill, if late payment is true, add a ten percent penalty. Return a list of final bills. Example input: [(1500, 'residential', False), (2000, 'commercial', True), (-1, 'none', False)] outputs [10.0, 121.0].

Write a function `boxoffice(patrons)` to process ticket sales. The input is a list of tuples with age, matinee boolean, and three d boolean. Process until age is zero. The standard base ticket price is fifteen dollars. If age is under twelve, the base price is ten dollars. If age is sixty five or older, the base price is twelve dollars. If matinee is true, subtract three dollars from this base price. If three d is true, add four dollars to the total. The three d surcharge is always four dollars and is never discounted by matinee or age. Accumulate the total revenue for all patrons processed and return that sum. Example input: [(10, True, True), (30, False, True), (70, True, False), (0, False, False)] outputs 39.0.

Write a function `calories(sessions)` to track workouts. The input is a list of tuples with activity type string, duration in minutes, and average heart rate. Process until duration is zero. Activities are running, cycling, swimming, and yoga. Base burn rates per minute are ten for running, eight for cycling, nine for swimming, and four for yoga. For all activities except yoga, modify the rate based on heart rate: if heart rate is over one hundred fifty, increase the base burn rate by twenty percent. If heart rate is under one hundred, decrease it by ten percent. Multiply the final rate by duration. Return a list of total calories burned per session, rounded to the nearest integer. Example input: [('running', 30, 160), ('yoga', 60, 90), ('none', 0, 0)] outputs [360, 240].

Write a function `grade(score, late, absence)`. The score is a number, late is a boolean, and absence is an integer. If absence is more than five, the grade is a fail regardless of the score. If late is true, the score drops by ten before checking the grade brackets. If the final score is ninety or above, it is classified as excellent. If the score is between eighty and eighty nine, it is good. If the score is between seventy and seventy nine, it is a pass. Anything below seventy is a fail. Return a string representing the final classification.

Write a function `navigate(commands, grid)`. The commands input is a string of letters representing forward, backward, left, and right. The grid is a list of lists of integers where zero is empty space and one is a wall. The rover starts at coordinates zero zero facing east. Loop through each command. If the command is left or right, change the facing direction accordingly. If the command is forward or backward, calculate the new coordinates based on the current facing direction. If the new coordinate is outside the grid boundaries, ignore the move entirely. If the new coordinate contains a wall, stop processing immediately and return the current position. Return a tuple of the final row and column.

Write a function `filter(packets)`. The input is a list of tuples containing source address, destination port, and protocol string. Create an empty list for allowed traffic and loop through each packet. If the protocol is tcp and the port is eighty or four four three, allow it. If the protocol is udp and the port is fifty three, allow it. If the source address starts with ten dot or one nine two dot, drop it as internal traffic. If the port is twenty two and the source is not a specific trusted address, drop it. Add all allowed items to your list and return it.

Write a function `access(user, file, action)`. The user is a tuple of user id and group id. The file is a tuple of owner id, group id, and an integer representing permission bits. The action is a string like read, write, or execute. First check if the user id matches the file owner id. If so, shift the bits to check the owner permissions. If not, check if the group ids match. If they match, shift the bits for group permissions. If neither match, check the world permissions. If the action is read, check the fours bit. If write, check the twos bit. If execute, check the ones bit. Return a boolean indicating if access is granted.

Write a function `validate(stats, race, classname)`. Stats is a list of six integers. If any stat is below three or above eighteen, return false. If the race is elf, add two to the second stat. If the race is dwarf, add two to the third stat. If the race is orc, add two to the first and subtract two from the fourth. If the classname is wizard, the fourth stat must be at least fourteen. If the classname is fighter, the first or second stat must be at least fourteen. If the classname is rogue, the second stat must be at least fourteen. Return true if all class requirements are met and stats remain valid.

Write a function `predict(rainfall, temp, soil)`. Rainfall and temp are numbers, soil is a string. Start with a base yield of one hundred. If rainfall is below twenty, reduce yield by fifty percent. If rainfall is above eighty, reduce yield by twenty percent due to flooding. If temp is below fifteen, subtract thirty from the yield. If temp is above thirty five, subtract forty. If the soil is clay and rainfall is high, subtract another ten. If the soil is sandy and rainfall is low, subtract fifteen. If the soil is loam, add twenty to the final result. Return the final estimated yield as an integer.

Write a function `price(distance, time, passenger)`. Distance is a number, time is an integer representing hour of day, passenger is a string like adult, child, or senior. Base fare is distance multiplied by zero point two. If the time is between seven and nine or sixteen and eighteen, multiply the fare by one point five for peak hours. If the passenger is a child, apply a fifty percent discount. If the passenger is a senior and it is not peak hours, apply a thirty percent discount. If the calculated fare is less than five, set it to the minimum fare of five. If the distance is over two hundred, subtract ten for a long distance discount. Return the final price rounded to two decimal places.

Write a function `analyze(sequence)`. The input is a string of letters. First check if the string length is a multiple of three. If not, return an invalid length error string. Iterate through the string in chunks of three. If a chunk contains any letter other than a, c, g, or t, return an invalid character error. If the chunk is exactly a t g, increment a start counter. If the chunk is t a a, t a g, or t g a, increment a stop counter. If the start counter is zero and a stop chunk is found, return premature stop. If the sequence finishes with no stop chunks, return missing stop. Return a tuple of the two counters.

Write a function `scale(ingredients, multiplier)`. The ingredients input is a list of tuples containing amount, unit, and name. Loop through each item and multiply the amount by the multiplier. If the unit is teaspoon and the new amount is three or more, convert it to tablespoons by dividing by three. If the unit is tablespoon and the amount is sixteen or more, convert it to cups by dividing by sixteen. If the unit is ounces and the amount is sixteen or more, convert it to pounds. If the unit is cup and the amount is more than four, convert to quarts. Return a new list of scaled and converted ingredient tuples.

Write a function `commute(zones, transfers, time)`. Zones is an integer, transfers is an integer, time is a float representing the hour. The base cost is two dollars for one zone. If zones is two, add one dollar. If zones is three or more, add two dollars. If the time is between eight and ten in the morning, add a surcharge of fifty cents. If the time is after midnight and before five, add a night fee of one dollar. If transfers is exactly one, add twenty five cents. If transfers is two or more, add fifty cents. If the final total exceeds five dollars, cap it at five dollars. Return the final float value.

Write a function `translate(sentence)`. The input is a string of words separated by spaces. Split the sentence into words and process each one. If the word starts with a vowel like a, e, i, o, or u, append way to the end. If the word starts with a consonant cluster like ch, sh, or th, move the first two letters to the end and append ay. If the word starts with a single consonant, move it to the end and append ay. If the original word was capitalized, ensure the new word is capitalized. If the word contains numbers, leave it completely unchanged. Join the words back with spaces and return the string.

Write a function `water(moisture, humidity, species)`. Moisture and humidity are percentages as integers, species is a string. If the species is cactus and moisture is above ten, do not water. If the species is fern and moisture is below fifty, water immediately. If humidity is above eighty, reduce the standard watering amount by half. If humidity is below thirty, double the watering amount. If the species is orchid and moisture is below thirty, only water if humidity is also below forty. If the species is tomato and moisture is below forty, water immediately. Return a string indicating whether to water heavily, normally, lightly, or not at all.

Write a function `cipher(text, shift)`. The input is a string and an integer. Iterate through each character in the text. If the character is a vowel, shift it forward by the shift amount multiplied by two. If the character is a consonant, shift it forward by the normal shift amount. If the character is a digit, replace it with nine minus the digit. If the character is a space, replace it with an underscore. If the character is punctuation, leave it exactly as it is. If the alphabet shift goes past the letter z, wrap around to the start of the alphabet. Return the fully obfuscated string.

Write a function `score(word, squares)`. Word is a string, squares is a list of strings matching the word length indicating special tiles like double letter or triple word. Loop through each character. If the letter is a, e, i, o, or u, its base value is one. If it is z or q, its base value is ten. For other consonants assign standard values. If the corresponding square is double letter, multiply the letter value by two. If it is triple letter, multiply by three. Add the letter values to a running total. Finally, if any square was double word, multiply the entire total by two. If triple word, multiply by three. Return the final integer score.

Write a function `classify(keywords, length, agerating)`. Keywords is a list of strings, length is an integer page count, age rating is a string like adult or teen. If keywords contains spaceship or alien, set the base genre to sci fi. If keywords contains magic or dragon, set base genre to fantasy. If keywords contains murder or detective, set it to mystery. If the length is under one hundred, append novella to the genre. If the length is over five hundred, append epic. If the age rating is teen, prepend young adult to the output. If no keywords match, return general fiction. Return the constructed genre string.

Write a function `detect(amount, location, time)`. Amount is a float, location is a string country code, time is an integer hour. Set a threat score to zero. If the amount is over one thousand, add three to the score. If the amount is under one dollar, add one to the score. If the location is different from the home country, add four to the score. If the location is a known high risk country, add another two. If the time is between midnight and four in the morning, add three to the score. If the score is five or higher, return blocked. If the score is between three and four, return review. Otherwise return approved.

Write a function `feed(weight, species, activity)`. Weight is a float in kilos, species is a string, activity is a string like low, medium, or high. Base calories is weight multiplied by thirty. If the species is dog, add ten percent to the base. If the species is cat, subtract five percent. If activity is high, multiply the total by one point five. If activity is low, multiply by zero point eight. If the animal is a puppy or kitten, double the required calories. If the final calorie count is below one hundred, set it to one hundred to prevent starvation. Return the integer rounded calorie requirement.

Write a function `monitor(oxygen, power, crew)`. Oxygen and power are percentages, crew is an integer. If crew is zero, switch to standby mode. If oxygen is below twenty percent, trigger a critical alarm. If power is below fifteen percent, turn off non essential systems. If oxygen is dropping faster than expected and crew is more than two, activate backup scrubbers. If power is above ninety percent, charge emergency batteries. If both oxygen and power are below ten percent, initiate evacuation protocols. If all systems are above eighty percent and crew is active, return nominal. Return a string representing the current system status.

Write a function `score(dives)` that calculates the total points for a competition. The input is a list of tuples, where each tuple contains a difficulty multiplier, a list of judge scores, a dive position string, and a boolean flag indicating if a balk occurred. Loop through each dive to compute its points. If the dive has five judge scores, discard the single highest and lowest scores. If it has seven scores, discard the two highest and two lowest scores. If a balk occurred, deduct two points from the sum of the remaining scores. If the dive position is straight, add a bonus of one point to the sum. If the position is tucked, subtract half a point. If the dive position is free, add no bonus. If the remaining sum is negative, set it to zero. Finally, multiply the sum by the difficulty multiplier. If the final calculated score exceeds one hundred, cap it at exactly one hundred. Return a list of final scores for all dives evaluated.

Write a function `transfuse(requests)` that determines if blood donations are safe. The input is a list of tuples containing the donor blood type, donor rh factor, recipient blood type, and recipient rh factor. Loop through the requests to evaluate compatibility. If the donor is type O and rh negative, automatically mark the donation as safe since they are a universal donor. If the recipient is type AB and rh positive, automatically mark the donation as safe since they are a universal recipient. Otherwise, evaluate specific blood types. If the recipient is type AB, they can receive any ABO type. If the recipient is type O, they can only receive type O. If the recipient is type A, they can receive A or O. If the recipient is type B, they can receive B or O. For the rh factor, if the recipient is positive, they can receive positive or negative blood. If the recipient is negative, they can only receive negative blood. Both ABO and rh conditions must be met for the donation to be safe. Return a list of boolean values for each request.

Create a function `assess(fouls)` to determine disciplinary actions in a handball match. The input is a list of tuples describing foul events with the player name, contact type, and severity. Maintain a count of yellow cards and two minute suspensions per player. Loop through the fouls to process them. If the contact is to the head, issue a red card immediately. If the contact is from behind, issue a two minute suspension. If the foul is holding the shirt, issue a yellow card. If the foul involves verbal abuse of the referee, issue a red card. If the foul involves unsportsmanlike conduct, issue a two minute suspension. If the foul is a simple foot block, record it as a free throw with no card. If a player receives a yellow card but already has one, escalate it to a two minute suspension. If a player accumulates three two minute suspensions, escalate the final one to a red card. Return a list of actions taken for each foul in order.

Design a function `select(loads)` to choose the appropriate washing machine settings. The input is a list of tuples with fabric type, soil level, and color fastness. Evaluate each load to return a cycle string. If the fabric is silk or wool, select the delicate cycle. If the fabric is denim, select the heavy duty cold cycle. If the load contains waterproof jackets, select the gentle cold cycle. If the fabric is cotton and heavily soiled, select heavy duty warm. If the fabric is synthetic and lightly soiled, select permanent press. If the item is heavily soiled and synthetic, select warm permanent press. If the colors are known to bleed, select the cold wash cycle to prevent fading. If the load consists of white cotton, select the hot wash cycle. For all other combinations, default to a normal warm wash. If the soil level is extreme, append an extra rinse phase to the selected cycle name. Return a list of chosen cycles.

Create a function `balance(readings)` to automate aquarium maintenance. The input is a list of tuples representing current temperature, acidity, salinity, ammonia, nitrate, water level, and filter flow. For each reading, compile a list of necessary adjustments. If the temperature is below seventy five, add a command to turn on the heater. If it is above eighty two, add a command to turn on the chiller. If the acidity is below six point five, add a command to dose alkaline buffer. If the acidity is above seven point five, add a command to dose acid. If salinity drops below one point zero two, add a command to mix salt. If ammonia is strictly greater than zero, immediately append an emergency water change alert. If the nitrate level is above forty, add a command to schedule a routine water change. If the water level is marked as low, add a command to top off the tank. If the filter flow is restricted, add a command to clean the filter media. Return a list of adjustment lists for each reading.

Implement a function `advise(metrics)` that recommends gear shifts for a cyclist. The input is a list of tuples containing current cadence, gradient percentage, speed, terrain type, and rider posture. Evaluate each state to suggest an action. If the rider is sprinting, suggest shifting to the highest gear immediately. If standing on the pedals, suggest maintaining the current gear. If the cadence is above ninety and the gradient is flat, suggest a shift up. If the cadence is below seventy and the gradient is uphill, suggest a shift down. If the speed is over twenty and the gradient is downhill, suggest two shifts up. If the gradient is steep uphill and the speed is dropping rapidly, suggest a front derailleur shift down. If the speed is under five and the cyclist is approaching a stop, suggest shifting down to the lowest gear. If riding on gravel and the speed is high, suggest shifting down once for better torque. If a strong crosswind is detected, suggest shifting down to maintain control. Return a list of suggested actions.

Develop a function `judge(dogs)` to score competitors in a conformation show. The input is a list of tuples detailing the dog's height, weight, coat color, gait, ear posture, tail docking, and behavior. Start each dog with a perfect score of one hundred. If the height exceeds twenty inches, deduct five points. If the weight is under thirty pounds, deduct three points. If the coat color is non standard, record a disqualification and assign a score of zero. If the dog is pacing instead of trotting, deduct ten points for a movement fault. If the teeth are overshot, deduct two points. If the teeth are undershot, deduct eight points for a major fault. If the ears do not stand erect, deduct four points. If the tail is docked improperly, deduct six points. If the dog acts aggressively towards the judge, disqualify immediately and assign a score of zero. Return a list of final scores for all dogs evaluated.

Create a function `generate(parameters)` that builds musical scales. The input is a tuple with a starting note number and a string representing the mode. Start a list with the initial note. Loop exactly seven times to build an octave. If the mode is major, use the interval pattern of two, two, one, two, two, two, one half steps. If the mode is natural minor, use two, one, two, two, one, two, two. If the mode is harmonic minor, use the natural minor pattern but increase the seventh interval by one to create a leading tone. If the mode is melodic minor ascending, raise the sixth and seventh intervals of the natural minor. If the mode is dorian, use two, one, two, two, two, one, two. If the mode is phrygian, use one, two, two, two, one, two, two. If the mode is lydian, use two, two, two, one, two, two, one. Calculate each successive note by adding the current interval to the previous note. Return the list of eight notes.

Design a function `control(telemetry)` to output safety commands for an autonomous drone. The input is a list of tuples containing battery percentage, wind speed, distance to restricted airspace, payload weight, gps signal strength, and motor temperature. Process each telemetry frame. If the battery falls below fifteen percent, issue a return to home command. If the battery drops below five percent, issue an emergency land command immediately. If the wind speed exceeds twenty miles per hour, issue a reduce altitude command. If the distance to restricted airspace is under one hundred feet, issue a reverse course command. If the payload is heavy and the battery is draining rapidly, issue a reduce speed command to conserve power. If gps signal is lost, issue a hover in place command. If a collision avoidance sensor triggers, issue an evade upward command. If the motor temperature exceeds safe limits, issue a reduce throttle command. Return a list of generated flight commands.

Write a function `schedule(plants)` to determine daily greenhouse tasks. The input is a list of tuples containing plant species, soil moisture level, ambient humidity, forecast rain, and lifecycle stage. Loop through the plants. If the plant is a succulent, only schedule watering if the soil moisture is completely dry and the humidity is low. If it is a tropical plant, schedule watering if the topsoil is dry, regardless of humidity. If it is a fern, schedule watering if the soil is even slightly dry. If rain is forecast in the next twenty four hours, skip watering for any plants marked as outdoor. If the temperature exceeds ninety degrees, water all outdoor non succulents even if the soil is damp. If the plant is a newly propagated cutting, water lightly every single day regardless of soil. If the plant is an orchid, only water if the roots appear silvery gray. If the plant is dormant for the winter, skip watering entirely. Return a list of plants needing water.

Design a function `locate(items)` to assign warehouse bays to incoming freight. The input is a list of tuples detailing item weight, hazard class, refrigeration requirements, turnover rate, and fragility. Loop through the items. If the item is hazardous and flammable, assign it to the outdoor bunker. If it is hazardous and toxic, assign it to the secure locked cage. If the item requires refrigeration, assign it to the cold storage zone. If the item weighs over one hundred pounds, assign it to the bottom rack to prevent lifting injuries. If the item is lightweight and has a high turnover rate, assign it to the front shelves for easy access. If the item is oversized and cannot fit on a rack, assign it to floor loading. If the item is fragile, assign it to the padded safety shelves. If the item is high value, assign it to the security vault. If the item is biological material, assign it to the quarantine zone. Return a list of bay assignments.

Create a function `plow(roads)` to prioritize snow clearing operations. The input is a list of tuples specifying road type, current snow depth, hospital route status, time of day, and weather alerts. Loop over the roads. If the road is an arterial highway and snow depth is over two inches, assign it priority one. If the road is a designated hospital route, assign it priority one regardless of the snow depth. If the road is residential and the snow depth exceeds six inches, assign it priority two. If a residential road has under six inches of snow, assign it priority three. If the time of day is between midnight and five in the morning, suspend all priority three plowing and reassign them to standby status. If the road is a school bus route and the time is between six and eight in the morning, elevate to priority one. If the road is a steep hill and icing is reported, dispatch a salt truck before the plow. If a snow emergency is declared by the city, upgrade all residential roads to priority two. Return a list of assigned priorities.

Write a function `evaluate(arrows)` to score an archer's target practice. The input is a list of tuples containing the ring hit, a boolean indicating if it broke the line into the next ring, and sequence penalties. For each arrow, if it hits the center x ring, score it as ten points and record an x for tie breaking. If it hits the inner gold, award ten points. If it hits the outer gold, award nine points. If it hits the inner red, award eight. If it hits the outer red, award seven. If it hits the inner blue, award six. If it hits the outer blue, award five. If the arrow is a line breaker, increment its score by one to award the higher ring value, up to a maximum of ten. If the arrow misses the target entirely, award zero points. If the archer shoots out of sequence, deduct two points from the total. If the arrow bounces off the target face, record it as a re shoot instead of assigning points. Return a tuple containing the total score and the count of x ring hits.

Write a function `score(throws)` that calculates the remaining score in a game of darts starting from five hundred and one. The input is a list of tuples containing the target segment and a multiplier. A standard target is a number from one to twenty, which can have a multiplier of one, two, or three. The outer bullseye has a value of twenty-five and a multiplier of one, while the inner bullseye has a value of fifty and a multiplier of one. Subtract the value of each throw multiplied by its multiplier from the current score. If a throw reduces the score to exactly zero and has a multiplier of two or is the inner bullseye, the game is won. If a throw reduces the score to one, or below zero, or to exactly zero without a multiplier of two or inner bullseye, the throw is a bust and the score reverts to what it was before that turn began. Return the final score as an integer, or a string indicating a win. For example, passing throws of twenty with a multiplier of three, and twenty with a multiplier of one returns four hundred and twenty one.

Implement a function `track(points)` that takes a list of strings indicating which player won each point, either player one or player two. Both players start at zero points. Winning a point progresses their score from zero to fifteen, then thirty, then forty. If both players reach forty, the game enters deuce. From deuce, if a player wins a point, they gain the advantage. If the player with the advantage wins the next point, they win the game. If the other player wins the point instead, the score returns to deuce. If a player reaches forty and wins the next point while the other player is at thirty or less, they win the game outright. Return a string representing the current state of the game, such as player one wins, player two wins, deuce, advantage player one, advantage player two, or the numerical score like fifteen to thirty. For example, a sequence of four points won by player one returns the string player one wins.

Write a function `score(events)` that calculates the final points for two opposing rugby teams. The input is a list of tuples containing the scoring team as an integer one or two, and the event type as a string. A try awards five points. If a try is scored, the very next event might be a conversion by the same team, which awards two points. If a conversion is missed or the team scores something else next, no extra points are added for the conversion. A penalty kick awards three points. A drop goal awards three points. If an event type is a yellow card, the offending team loses one point as a disciplinary deduction. If an event type is a red card, they lose three points. If the total points for a team drops below zero due to penalties, cap their score at zero. Keep a running tally for both teams. Return a tuple containing the final score of team one and team two.

Write a function `price(attributes)` that calculates the cost of a daily ski pass. The base price is one hundred dollars. The input is a list containing the skier's age, the season, the days booked in advance, whether they are a local resident, and whether they are a student. If the age is under twelve or over sixty-five, apply a fifty percent discount to the base price. If the season is peak, add a twenty dollar surcharge, but if it is spring, deduct ten dollars. If the ticket is booked more than thirty days in advance, apply a twenty percent discount on the current subtotal, or if it is booked between seven and thirty days in advance, apply a ten percent discount. Finally, if the skier is a local resident, deduct fifteen dollars from the total. If they are a student, deduct ten dollars. Only one of the resident or student discounts can be applied, preferring the resident discount. Return the final price rounded to the nearest dollar.

Implement a function `validate(catch)` that checks if a caught fish is legal to keep. The input is a list containing the species name, length in centimeters, the current month, the location type, and the angler license tier. For a salmon, the length must be at least fifty centimeters, and it can only be caught between May and September inclusive. For a bass, the length must be between thirty and forty-five centimeters, and it is illegal to catch in marine locations. For a trout, the length must be at least twenty-five centimeters, and catching them requires a premium license tier. If the location type is protected, all fishing is strictly catch and release regardless of species. If any of these conditions are violated, return a string indicating the specific reason for rejection, such as undersized, out of season, protected area, or insufficient license. If all rules are satisfied, return the string approved.

Write a function `handicap(data)` that calculates the corrected time for a sailboat in a race. The input is a list containing the boat class, elapsed time in minutes, average wind speed in knots, a false start penalty flag, and the number of buoys touched. The base corrected time is the elapsed time. If the boat class is laser, multiply the time by a rating of zero point nine. If the class is catamaran, multiply by zero point eight. If the class is dinghy, multiply by one point one. Next, adjust for wind conditions. If the wind speed is below five knots, add a five percent penalty to the time because heavier boats struggle more. If the wind speed is above twenty knots, subtract five percent from the time. Add five minutes to the time for every buoy touched. Finally, if the false start flag is true, add an additional ten minutes to the time. Return the final corrected time rounded to one decimal place.

Create a function `monitor(telemetry)` that evaluates the health of a descending spacecraft. The input is a list of five numbers representing altitude in kilometers, velocity in meters per second, heat shield temperature in celsius, fuel percentage, and communication signal strength. Start with an empty list of warning messages. If altitude is below fifty and velocity is greater than two thousand, append a velocity warning. If the heat shield temperature exceeds one thousand five hundred, append a critical temperature warning, or if it is below minus fifty, append a freezing warning. If the fuel percentage drops below ten, append a low fuel warning. If the communication signal strength is below twenty, append a signal loss warning. If the list of warnings is empty, check if altitude is zero and velocity is less than ten, and if so return a list containing only a safe landing message, otherwise return a list containing only nominal. Otherwise, return the accumulated list of warnings.

Write a function `load(vehicles)` that calculates the layout of vehicles on a ferry. The input is a list of tuples containing vehicle type, length in meters, weight in tons, and a hazardous cargo flag. The ferry has a main deck with a fifty meter lane and a lower deck with a forty meter lane, and a total weight capacity of one hundred tons. If a vehicle has hazardous cargo, it must be placed on the main deck regardless of size. If the vehicle is a truck and weighs more than ten tons, it must also go on the main deck. If the vehicle is a passenger car, it prefers the lower deck. If the preferred or required deck is full, meaning the sum of lengths exceeds the lane capacity, it attempts to go to the other deck, unless it is restricted. If both decks are full or restricted, the vehicle is rejected. If the vehicle's weight alone exceeds the remaining total weight capacity of the ferry, it is rejected. Return a list of tuples containing the accepted vehicles and their assigned decks.

Create a function `wash(settings)` that generates a sequence of washing stages. The input is a list containing the package type, dirt level, and vehicle size. The available packages are basic, standard, and premium. Always start the sequence with an undercarriage spray. If the dirt level is high, append a heavy pre-soak stage, otherwise append a standard pre-soak, unless the package is basic and the dirt level is low and the size is small, in which case skip the pre-soak entirely. Next, append a soap application. If the vehicle size is large, append an extended scrubbing stage, otherwise append a regular scrubbing stage. After scrubbing, append a high pressure rinse. If the package is standard or premium, append a tire cleaning stage and a wax application. If the package is premium, additionally append a ceramic coating stage. Finally, if the vehicle size is small, append a standard dry, but if the vehicle size is large or the package is premium, append an extended heated dry. Return the list of stages in order.

Create a function `classify(contacts)` that evaluates an array of underwater sonar contacts. The input is a list of tuples containing signal strength, acoustic frequency in hertz, movement speed in knots, and depth in meters. If the signal strength is below ten, ignore the contact as background noise and do not add it to the results. If the speed is zero and depth is exactly zero, classify it as a surface buoy. If the speed is above thirty knots and depth is greater than fifty meters, classify it as a torpedo. If the frequency is between twenty and fifty hertz and the speed is between five and fifteen knots, classify it as a whale. If the frequency is above one thousand hertz and the depth is less than twenty meters, classify it as a small watercraft. If the speed is between ten and twenty knots, the depth is below one hundred meters, and the frequency is below two hundred hertz, classify it as a submarine. For any other combination that is not ignored, classify it as an unknown anomaly. Return a list of classifications in the order the valid contacts were received.

Create a function `dispense(order)` that calculates the required amounts of base paint and colorants in milliliters. The input is a list containing the desired color name, the finish type, and the total volume requested. Start with the entire volume as the base paint. If the finish is gloss, subtract ten percent of the volume from the base and assign it to gloss additive. If the finish is matte, subtract five percent from the base for a flattening agent. If the finish is satin, subtract two percent for a smoothing agent. If the color is crimson, add ten milliliters of red colorant and two milliliters of blue colorant for every liter of total volume requested. If the color is mint, add five milliliters of green and one milliliter of yellow per liter. If the color is navy, add twelve milliliters of blue and three milliliters of black per liter. If the color is mustard, add eight milliliters of yellow and two of brown per liter. If the total requested volume is over twenty liters, apply a five percent bulk discount reduction to the colorant amounts added. Ensure the base paint volume is finally adjusted by subtracting the total volume of all added colorants. Return a list of tuples containing the ingredient names and their calculated volumes.

Implement a function `check(parameters)` that verifies if a helicopter is safe to take off. The input is a list containing main rotor RPM, tail rotor RPM, engine temperature in celsius, oil pressure in PSI, and wind speed in knots. If the engine temperature is below forty degrees, return a message to warm up the engine. If the engine temperature is above one hundred and ten degrees, return a message to shut down due to overheating. If the oil pressure is below fifty PSI, return a low oil pressure warning. If the wind speed exceeds thirty-five knots, return a weather hold message. If the main rotor RPM is below three hundred, or the tail rotor RPM is below one thousand five hundred, return a spooling up message indicating they have not reached flight speed. If all these checks pass, and the wind speed is between twenty and thirty-five knots, return a marginal weather caution message. If all checks pass and winds are calm, return clear for takeoff.

Write a function `calibrate(observation)` that determines adjustments for an automated telescope. The input is a list containing the target type, tracking mode, atmospheric seeing quality, installed filter, and moon phase. The target types are planet, nebula, or galaxy. If the target is a planet, set the focal length to long and tracking to planetary. If the target is a nebula or galaxy, set the focal length to short and tracking to sidereal. If the atmospheric seeing is poor, append an instruction to activate adaptive optics. If the seeing is excellent, append an instruction to bypass adaptive optics. If the target is a nebula and the filter is none, append an instruction to insert a narrowband filter. If the target is a planet and the filter is narrowband, append an instruction to switch to a color filter. If the filter installed is infrared and the target is not a planet, append an instruction to remove the infrared filter. If the target is a galaxy and the moon phase is full, append a light pollution warning. If the provided tracking mode does not match the required tracking determined by the target, append a tracking mismatch warning. Return a list of all determined instructions and warnings.

Implement a function `score(balls)` that calculates the points scored in a single continuous turn of snooker. The input is a list of strings representing the colors of the balls potted in order. A red ball is worth one point, yellow two, green three, brown four, blue five, pink six, and black seven. The sequence must alternate between red and any other color. If a red is expected but a non-red is potted, the break ends immediately and no points are added for that foul shot. If a color is expected but a red is potted, the break also ends. Once all reds are gone, which you can assume is after exactly fifteen reds have been potted in the break, the colors must be potted in strictly ascending order of their value. If a ball is potted out of sequence during this final phase, the break ends. Accumulate the values of all legally potted balls and return the total score as an integer.

Write a function `track(actions)` that determines the points awarded in a fencing exchange. The input is a list of strings representing a sequence of actions, such as attack left, attack right, parry left, parry right, touch left, touch right, and off target. In foil fencing, a touch only scores if the fencer has right of way. An attack establishes right of way for that fencer. A parry transfers right of way to the defender. If a fencer with right of way lands a touch, they score one point and the exchange ends. If they land an off target, the exchange ends with no points. If a fencer lands a touch without right of way, it is ignored unless the fencer with right of way missed completely or went off target. If both attack simultaneously without a parry and both touch, it is a simultaneous action and no points are awarded. Process the sequence to track right of way and return a tuple of points scored by the left fencer and the right fencer.

Create a function `evaluate(routine)` that calculates the technical score for a figure skating program. The input is a list of tuples, each containing an element name, a base value, a grade of execution from minus five to plus five, and a fall flag. For each element, start with the base value. If the grade of execution is positive, add ten percent of the base value for each grade point. If the grade of execution is negative, subtract ten percent of the base value for each grade point. If the fall flag is true, subtract a mandatory one point from the element's score, and cap the grade of execution at a maximum of minus three before calculating its penalty. If an element's final score drops below zero, set it to zero. Furthermore, if the element name contains the word jump and occurs in the second half of the routine, indicated by being past the middle index of the list, multiply its base value by one point one before applying execution grades. Return the total score rounded to two decimal places.

Implement a function `advise(scene)` that recommends camera settings based on scene characteristics. The input is a list containing the light level in lux, subject speed in kilometers per hour, and desired depth of field as shallow or deep. Start with an ISO of one hundred, an aperture of point f eight, and a shutter speed of one two hundredth of a second. If the subject speed is above fifty, change the shutter speed to one one thousandth and increase the ISO to eight hundred. If the subject speed is between ten and fifty, change the shutter speed to one five hundredth and increase the ISO to four hundred. If the subject speed is zero, change the shutter speed to one fiftieth. Next, adjust for depth of field. If shallow is desired, change the aperture to point f two point eight and halve the ISO, ensuring it does not drop below one hundred. If deep is desired, change the aperture to point f sixteen and double the ISO. Finally, if the light level is below one thousand lux, double the ISO again. If the light level is below one hundred lux, require a tripod and change the shutter speed to one full second, while setting the aperture to point f one point four. Return a list of the final ISO, aperture, and shutter speed.

Write a function `route(baggage)` that determines the correct conveyor chute for a piece of luggage. The input is a list containing the destination code, weight in kilograms, length in centimeters, priority class, a fragile flag, and security scan status. If the security scan status is fail, immediately route the bag to the manual inspection chute regardless of other attributes. If the length exceeds one hundred and twenty centimeters or the weight exceeds thirty-two kilograms, route the bag to the oversized freight chute. If the bag is tagged as fragile and is not oversized, route it to the fragile handling belt regardless of its destination code. For normal bags, if the priority class is first or business, append the priority tag to the routing instruction. If the priority class is economy but the weight is less than ten kilograms, append an express tag. If the destination code is local, meaning it starts with the letter L, route it to carousel one. If the destination code is domestic, starting with D, route it to carousel two. If the destination code is international, starting with I, route it to carousel three. Return a string combining the tag if applicable and the destination carousel or chute name.

Create a function `negotiate(status)` that determines the charging current in amps for an electric vehicle. The input is a list containing the current battery percentage, battery temperature in celsius, cable max rating in amps, and the station power limit in amps. The absolute maximum current is the lower of the cable rating and the station limit. If the battery temperature exceeds forty-five degrees, the current must be set to zero for safety. If the temperature is below zero degrees, the current is limited to a maximum of ten amps to prevent lithium plating. If the temperature is safe, look at the battery percentage. If the percentage is above eighty, the current is limited to twenty amps to protect battery health. If the percentage is above ninety-five, the current is limited to five amps for trickle charging. If the percentage is below eighty and the temperature is safe, allow the absolute maximum current. Return the final negotiated current as an integer.

Write a module to group triathlon participants into starting waves. The entry function `assign(athletes)` takes a list of tuples containing age, gender, and swim time in minutes. If gender is male and age under thirty, assign to wave one if swim time is under thirty minutes. If male and age thirty to fifty, assign to wave two if swim time is under thirty five minutes. If male and age over fifty, assign to wave three. If gender is female and age under thirty, assign to wave four if swim time is under thirty two minutes. If female and age thirty to fifty, assign to wave five. If female and age over fifty, assign to wave six. If swim time is over sixty minutes regardless of age or gender, assign to the final wave. Otherwise assign to the open wave. Return a list of wave assignment strings. Example: `[(25, "male", 28)]` returns `["wave one"]`.

Generate automated alerts based on radar storm signatures. The entry function `warn(readings)` takes a list of tuples containing rotation speed, a boolean for funnel visible, and a string for radar echo type. If rotation speed exceeds one hundred and funnel visible is true, issue a tornado emergency. If rotation speed exceeds one hundred and funnel visible is false, issue a tornado warning. If radar echo is debris ball regardless of rotation, issue a catastrophic tornado emergency. If rotation speed is between sixty and one hundred and radar echo is hook, issue a tornado warning. If rotation speed is between sixty and one hundred and radar echo is bow, issue a severe thunderstorm warning. If rotation speed is between twenty and sixty and radar echo is hook, issue a severe weather statement. If rotation speed is under sixty and funnel visible is true, issue a spotter investigation request. If radar echo is clear and rotation speed is under twenty, issue an all clear. Otherwise issue a weather watch. Return a list of alert strings. Example: `[(120, True, "hook")]` returns `["tornado emergency"]`.

Choose the correct objective lens and filter based on biological sample properties. The entry function `select(samples)` takes a list of tuples containing sample type, staining method, and desired magnification. If sample type is bacteria and desired magnification is one thousand, select the oil immersion objective lens. If sample type is bacteria and desired magnification is four hundred, select the high power dry lens. If sample type is tissue slice and staining is fluorescent, select the ultraviolet filter block and low power lens. If sample type is living cells and staining is none, select the phase contrast lens. If desired magnification is forty and sample type is insect, select the stereomicroscope macro lens. If sample type is crystal and staining is polarized, select the polarization filter lens. If staining is darkfield and desired magnification is over two hundred, select the specialized darkfield condenser lens. If sample type is blood smear, always select the standard high power lens. Otherwise select the general ten times objective lens. Return a list of lens strings. Example: `[("bacteria", "none", 1000)]` returns `["oil immersion objective lens"]`.

Provide care instructions for different types of greenhouse orchids. The entry function `guide(orchids)` takes a list of tuples containing genus, leaf color, root health, and humidity percentage. If genus is phalaenopsis and leaf color is dark green, increase light exposure immediately. If genus is phalaenopsis and root health is brown, stop watering and apply fungicide. If genus is cattleya and humidity is below forty, add a humidifier and mist daily. If genus is cattleya and leaf color is yellow, reduce light exposure. If genus is vanda and root health is silvery, water heavily until roots turn green. If genus is paphiopedilum and leaf color is pale, apply a weak magnesium fertilizer. If genus is dendrobium and humidity is above eighty, increase air circulation to prevent rot. If root health is mushy regardless of genus, unpot and trim dead roots immediately. Otherwise maintain current care routine. Return a list of care strings. Example: `[("phalaenopsis", "dark green", "green", 50)]` returns `["increase light exposure immediately"]`.

Recommend interventions for beekeepers based on hive inspection data. The entry function `inspect(colonies)` takes a list of tuples containing mite count, brood pattern string, honey stores string, and weather condition. If mite count is over ten and brood pattern is spotty, recommend immediate varroa treatment. If mite count is over ten and brood pattern is solid, recommend varroa monitoring and gentle treatment. If brood pattern is spotty and honey stores are low, recommend feeding pollen substitute and sugar syrup. If brood pattern is solid and honey stores are high, recommend adding a honey super box. If honey stores are very low and weather is cold, recommend emergency winter fondant feeding. If weather is stormy and honey stores are high, recommend adding a heavy roof weight. If mite count is zero and brood pattern is solid, recommend no action needed. If brood pattern is completely absent, recommend requeening the hive immediately. Otherwise recommend standard weekly inspection. Return a list of recommendation strings. Example: `[(12, "spotty", "high", "warm")]` returns `["immediate varroa treatment"]`.

Determine the optimal binding setup for a snowboarder. The entry function `calculate(riders)` takes a list of tuples containing height in centimeters, riding style, boot size, and experience level. If riding style is freestyle and experience is beginner, set stance width to fifty centimeters and angles to zero. If riding style is freestyle and experience is advanced, set stance width to fifty five centimeters and angles to duck stance. If riding style is freeride and height is over one hundred eighty, set stance width to sixty centimeters and angles to positive directional. If riding style is freeride and height is under one hundred eighty, set stance width to fifty two centimeters. If riding style is alpine and experience is advanced, set stance to forward racing angles. If boot size is over eleven, add wide board requirement and increase angles by three degrees. If boot size is under seven, add narrow board requirement. If experience is expert regardless of style, suggest custom micro adjustments. Otherwise set stance to standard fifty centimeters and mild positive angles. Return a list of stance strings. Example: `[(170, "freestyle", 9, "beginner")]` returns `["fifty centimeters and angles to zero"]`.

Monitor and direct the progress of fermenting beverages. The entry function `validate(batches)` takes a list of tuples containing ph level, temperature in celsius, gravity string, and days active. If ph level is below four and gravity is stable, mark batch as complete and ready for bottling. If ph level is above five and days active is over seven, mark batch as stalled and add yeast nutrient. If temperature is over thirty five and days active is over three, mark batch as heat damaged and discard. If temperature is over thirty and ph level is below four, mark batch as at risk of fusel alcohols and chill immediately. If temperature is under fifteen and gravity is dropping slowly, mark batch as slow ferment and warm the vessel. If days active is over fourteen and gravity is not stable, mark batch as struggling and rouse the yeast. If ph level is below three point two, mark batch as overly acidic and consider blending. If gravity is extremely high and days active is zero, mark batch as ready to pitch yeast. Otherwise mark batch as actively fermenting. Return a list of status strings. Example: `[(3.8, 20, "stable", 10)]` returns `["ready for bottling"]`.

Recommend the correct heavy machinery attachment for earthmoving tasks. The entry function `select(jobs)` takes a list of tuples containing soil type, digging depth, a boolean for rocks present, and a boolean for precision needed. If soil type is clay and rocks present is true, select the heavy duty rock bucket with teeth. If soil type is clay and rocks present is false, select the standard digging bucket. If soil type is sand and digging depth is shallow, select the wide grading bucket. If soil type is sand and precision needed is true, select the tilt bucket. If soil type is gravel and digging depth is shallow, select the skeleton sifting bucket. If rocks present is true and precision needed is true, select the hydraulic thumb attachment. If digging depth is very deep and soil type is loose, select the long reach boom extension. If soil type is frozen, select the hydraulic breaker attachment immediately. Otherwise select the general purpose bucket. Return a list of attachment strings. Example: `[("clay", "deep", True, False)]` returns `["heavy duty rock bucket with teeth"]`.

Provide step mashing instructions for brewing beer. The entry function `direct(mashes)` takes a list of tuples containing beer style, malt type, target body, and current temperature. If beer style is stout and target body is full, raise temperature to sixty eight degrees for alpha amylase extraction. If beer style is pilsner and target body is light, lower temperature to sixty four degrees for beta amylase extraction. If beer style is sour and target body is light, lower temperature to sixty degrees for a prolonged rest. If malt type is wheat and current temp is under fifty, perform a ferulic acid rest at forty five degrees. If malt type is unmalted adjunct and current temp is under eighty, perform a cereal mash at eighty five degrees. If target body is medium and current temp is sixty six, maintain current temperature for saccharification. If beer style is hazy ipa and malt type is oats, raise temperature to sixty nine degrees. If current temp is over seventy five, initiate mash out to denature enzymes. Otherwise maintain sixty five degrees. Return a list of instruction strings. Example: `[("stout", "pale", "full", 60)]` returns `["raise temperature to sixty eight degrees"]`.

Assign transmission frequencies to communications dishes based on environmental factors. The entry function `allocate(links)` takes a list of tuples containing rain fade risk, bandwidth needed, dish size, and priority level.
